name: Root
description: Zero-props compositional root component that serves as the application entry point for the exemplar.tools documentation website. Instantiates the Convex real-time client from VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable (fail-fast on missing), composes the provider tree (ConvexProvider → BrowserRouter), and declares the route table with three routes inside app_shell's Layout wrapper: '/' → HomePage, '/:toolSlug' → ToolPage, '*' → redirect to '/'. Contains no business logic, no state, no effects — purely a provider and route composition layer. File budget is ≤50 lines. StrictMode wrapping is owned by main.tsx (project_scaffold), not this component; Root is rendered inside StrictMode.

functions.name: Root
functions.description: Zero-props React functional component (React.FC) exported as the default export from src/App.tsx (or src/Root.tsx). Composes the full provider and route tree: (1) reads VITE_CONVEX_URL at module scope and passes it to createConvexClient to obtain the singleton ConvexReactClient, (2) wraps the route tree in ConvexProvider with the client instance, (3) wraps in BrowserRouter for client-side routing, (4) declares a parent Route with element={<Layout />} containing three child routes: index route rendering HomePage, '/:toolSlug' route rendering ToolPage, and '*' catch-all route rendering <Navigate to='/' replace />. This component is rendered inside React.StrictMode by main.tsx — it does not itself wrap in StrictMode. File is ≤50 lines.

preconditions: import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL is defined and is a non-empty string (validated at module load time before Root is ever called)
createConvexClient from app_shell has successfully returned a ConvexReactClient instance (module-level singleton)
HomePage component is importable from home_page module
ToolPage component is importable from tool_page module
renderLayout (Layout component) is importable from app_shell module
React Router v6 Routes, Route, Navigate, and BrowserRouter are importable from react-router-dom
Component is rendered inside React.StrictMode by main.tsx (project_scaffold)
postconditions: Returns a single JSX tree: ConvexProvider > BrowserRouter > Routes > Route(path='/', element=Layout) with children
Layout route contains exactly three child routes: (1) index route → HomePage, (2) path=':toolSlug' → ToolPage, (3) path='*' → Navigate to='/' replace
ConvexProvider receives the singleton client instance from createConvexClient
No useState, useEffect, or any React hook is called within this component — it is purely compositional
No props are required or accepted
All routes are reachable: '/' renders HomePage inside Layout, '/:toolSlug' renders ToolPage inside Layout, any unmatched path redirects to '/'
The catch-all '*' route uses <Navigate to='/' replace /> so unrecognized paths redirect to home without adding a history entry

structured_side_effects.description: Root is purely compositional — no side effects. Provider setup and client instantiation happen at module scope, not within the component function body.

functions.name: getRouteTable
functions.description: Pure function that returns the canonical route table metadata as a RouteTable array. Documents the three routes declared by Root for testing and introspection purposes. Not used at runtime by Root itself — exists for contract verifiability and test assertions.
postconditions: Element 0: { path: '/', component: 'HomePage', isIndex: true, isCatchAll: false }
Element 1: { path: '/:toolSlug', component: 'ToolPage', isIndex: false, isCatchAll: false }
Element 2: { path: '*', component: 'Navigate', isIndex: false, isCatchAll: true }

invariants: Root component accepts zero props — it is typed as React.FC with no generic parameter (equivalent to React.FC<{}>)
Exactly one ConvexReactClient instance exists per application lifecycle, instantiated at module scope via createConvexClient from app_shell — Root does not create its own client
The route table contains exactly three child routes under the Layout parent: index (HomePage), :toolSlug (ToolPage), and * (Navigate redirect to '/')
Root does not wrap in React.StrictMode — that responsibility belongs to main.tsx (project_scaffold)
Root contains no useState, useEffect, useContext, or any React hook calls — it is purely a composition of providers and routes
Root file is ≤50 lines of source code
Root does not define any new domain types — all domain types (ToolSlug, ToolDef, Comment, etc.) are imported from dependency modules
VITE_CONVEX_URL validation happens at module load time (top-level scope), not inside the Root component function body — this ensures fail-fast behavior before any rendering attempt
The catch-all '*' route uses <Navigate to='/' replace /> — it redirects to home without adding a browser history entry
The :toolSlug route parameter name matches the app_shell ROUTES.TOOL pattern ('/:toolSlug') so that ToolPage's useParams().toolSlug resolves correctly
Provider nesting order is always ConvexProvider (outermost) → BrowserRouter → Routes/Route tree (innermost) — Convex context must be available to all routed components

data_access.rationale: Root reads the VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable (classified INTERNAL — it is a deployment configuration secret containing the Convex backend URL) at module load time to initialize the Convex client. Root itself does not read or write any user data, PII, or PUBLIC data. All data access to the Convex backend (comments, tool definitions) is delegated to child components (CommentsSection via data_layer, HomePage/ToolPage via data_layer) which declare their own data access classifications.

side_effects.rationale: Reads the Convex deployment URL from Vite environment variables at module scope to pass to createConvexClient. This URL is an internal infrastructure configuration value, not user data.

authority.rationale: Root is the single authoritative owner of the application route table. It defines the exact set of route patterns ('/', '/:toolSlug', '*'), their mapping to page components (HomePage, ToolPage, Navigate), and the layout wrapper (Layout). No other component may define top-level routes. app_shell provides the ROUTES constant object and Layout component, but Root is the component that instantiates the actual React Router <Routes> tree with those patterns.
